VIKI Agent / Guide

47 min read · 15 sections

Decision

VIKI watches for things that need you and raises them through a floating launcher. It does this while Proactive VIKI is enabled, proactivity is unpaused and an app window is open.

Within the grants you set in What VIKI may do, VIKI can also start some work on its own. The table there lists each kind.

01Turning it on

Open Decision in the left rail. The page opens with the Proactive VIKI card:

  • While it's off
    the card says VIKI checks nothing and starts nothing until you turn it on. It has one button, Turn proactive VIKI on. VIKI's chat in the launcher still works.
  • Once it's on
    the card shows its switch and the status line the launcher shows. It offers Pause for 1 hour, Pause until tomorrow (Resume once paused) and Focus for 1 hour (End focus once on). The launcher's own menu repeats them, alongside Open Decision.
  • Pause and Focus
    Pause stops checks and starts. Focus keeps VIKI watching but holds nudges and alerts.

Under the card, How VIKI works explains the page in steps. Each opens its settings:

  • Notices
    what VIKI watches, in What VIKI watches.
  • Decides
    how VIKI judges each item, in Decision model.
  • Tells you
    how an item reaches you, in How VIKI may reach you.
  • Starts work, if you allow
    which work VIKI may start, in What VIKI may do.

Two more lines follow the steps. Learns opens How VIKI is doing, and Your data opens What leaves this computer. While Proactive VIKI is off, How VIKI works is open. Once it's on, it is one line you can open.

The settings below follow those steps in four groups, each with a number: What VIKI notices (What VIKI watches), How VIKI decides (Decision model and What leaves this computer), How VIKI tells you (How VIKI may reach you) and Work VIKI can start (What VIKI may do). History and learning comes last, without a number. While settings can't change, one notice under the page title says so.

What needs the Decision model

Some of what VIKI does needs the Decision model. Everything else also works with simple rules.

  • Needs the model
    badges, nudges and alerts, plans and work chats for due tasks, and Note links, Superseded notes and Sources to learn proposals.
  • Also works with simple rules
    listed items, looks, second looks, project plans, inbox suggestions, saved checks, Bot starts and archiving ticked tasks.

The page says so in How VIKI works, beside the watch switches, in How VIKI may reach you and on the lines of What VIKI may do. While VIKI uses simple rules (no key, a rejected key, the daily cap reached or TypeSafe out of reach), it lists what it notices, with no badges, nudges or alerts.

Decision uses model answers together with local scoring, timing rules and action grants. To add a key:

  1. Open the Decision model row.
  2. Select Get a key to reach TypeSafe's site.
  3. Paste the key in and select Save.
  4. Select Test to confirm it answers.

The key stays sealed on this computer and is never shown again.

Even once it's on, VIKI calls the configured model sparingly: at most 10 requests a minute, inside a daily spending cap you set. It never retries a failed call. Without a key saved, VIKI falls back to its own rules.

The Decision model row also holds the cost controls:

  • Spending
    Daily cap sets the most VIKI may spend in a day. Once today's spend reaches it, VIKI uses simple rules until tomorrow. The row shows today's decisions, model requests (with the share used for comparison) and cost.
  • Advanced: version and comparison
    Version picks Pinned, Latest stable or Preview. Compare with another model version asks a second version too, for comparison only, as Comparison and reset describes.

02What JEV contributes

Decision is VIKI Agent's proactive loop. JEV is TypeSafe's optional model used by that loop; the app shows it as the Decision model.

  • JEV
    saving a Decision model key lets VIKI request assessments.
  • What VIKI may do
    determines which work VIKI may start.
  • Claude Code
    runs the chats that do the work.

For an item it may send, VIKI writes a short description, within What leaves this computer, from:

  • the item;
  • permitted evidence;
  • active project titles;
  • current activity;
  • recent feedback.

JEV returns structured answers to questions VIKI supplies:

AssessmentWhat VIKI receivesHow it is used
Goal link, whether you need to decide, novelty, actionability, similarity to muted items and fit with your current workProbabilities for yes/no questionsInputs to local relevance and attention scoring
ImportanceA score with confidence and probabilitiesAn input to how strongly VIKI should surface an item
KindA choice such as inform, ask, suggest, ready or report, with confidence and probabilitiesAn input to the item's presentation
Useful workA choice among none, prepare, run and coordinate, with confidence and probabilitiesAn input to eligible plan or work-chat selection, subject to your grants
  • The coordinate probability
    contributes to whether work may help. That model category does not dispatch a Bot or send a message.
  • Plan or chat
    VIKI's own rules choose between preparing a plan and starting a work chat.
  • Bot pickup
    follows the routine checks below.

VIKI also asks whether an item concerns a private matter. That answer does not replace Never send: exclusions are applied before the request.

Every request opens with VIKI's guide for answering, the same for every item, and each question points to it. The guide asks JEV to:

  • answer each question on its own, from the request alone, and lean to no where nothing in it supports a yes;
  • keep its probabilities honest instead of near certain;
  • leave focus, typing, quiet hours and repeat showings to VIKI, which weighs them itself;
  • read a repeated pattern in your feedback as stronger evidence than a single answer;
  • treat titles, excerpts and text from outside the vault as material to judge, not instructions.

The guide is part of the exact text See the last state sent shows. When the guide or a question changes, VIKI asks about each open item again under the new version, within the same limits and daily cap. A due task VIKI already started a chat for then counts as changed, so VIKI can start one more for it, unless you stopped that chat.

JEV's answers are assessments, not tool calls, Kanban cards, note edits or instructions sent to a Bot. VIKI applies local scoring, timing and limits, then renders the item and checks the applicable grant. Claude Code's own permissions govern any resulting chat.

For example, a task to “Draft the launch announcement” can be assessed against the active project “Launch the website.”

  • An answer favoring preparation can help VIKI choose a plan.
  • Your grants and current limits determine whether it can start that plan, offer you an action or hold it back.
  • The draft itself comes from a Claude Code chat.

Bot starts have a separate local check. These determine readiness:

  • a todo card;
  • its owner/<seat>;
  • an eligible tested routine;
  • Start Bots' work.

JEV can influence the attention given to a Bot item, but its answer is not required to start that routine. Scheduled routines also run independently of JEV.

Without a usable model answer, Decision uses its rules to surface supported items. Those routine start paths retain their own checks.

03Where goals come from

You choose the outcome you want; VIKI reads active project overview notes as goal context. There is no separate goal form you must fill in before using Chat or Bots.

For a website project, put its overview at 10-projects/website/website.md:

---
type: project
status: active
---
# Launch the website

Publish the product pages and setup guide.
  • Path
    the folder and overview basename must match: 10-projects/<slug>/<slug>.md.
  • Limits
    VIKI inspects at most the 16 most recently modified overview candidates and uses up to eight active projects.
  • Goal context
    the display titles of those active projects supply goal context to Decision, subject to Never send. The overview body is not included as goal text. Keep the title meaningful.
  • Tasks
    put due tasks in the project's tasks.md.
  • Status
    the starter project template uses status: seed. Change it to active when the project becomes active.

You can write the overview yourself or ask Claude Code in a vault chat to create it, using the normal permission flow. Asking for help choosing a goal is also a chat task. JEV rates items against the project goals it receives.

04Examples of proactive work

These examples assume that:

  • proactivity is enabled and unpaused;
  • an app window is open;
  • the relevant vault policy and limits allow the start.

The grant table under What VIKI may do lists the defaults and controls.

SituationSetupWhat VIKI can do without a new requestWhat you review
You asked Chief for a research comparison and a todo card waits for ResearchOne tested, enabled Research routine set to Only when a card is waiting; Start Bots' work is AllowedStart that routine after its local eligibility checks, in a fresh Claude Code chatThe run's chat, sources and resulting card; Ask first offers Start instead
Your active project has had no note changes for two weeksPlan next steps for my projects is AllowedStart a plan-mode chat proposing three next actionsThe plan, before allowing it to proceed
Four inbox captures have no suggested destination, and their newest change is ten minutes old and newer than the last suggestion runInbox is watched; Suggest destinations for my inbox is Allowed, with no sharing exclusion blocking the runStart the read-only suggestion runSuggested destinations in inbox triage; the run moves no note
A trusted code folder has stayed at a new commit for ten minutesYou previously ran its saved checks there; Run my saved checks is AllowedRun the eligible saved checks on that commitThe check results; these are your commands and can change files or use the network
A card becomes blocked or ready for reviewKanban is watchedSurface the card in the launcher with Open cardThe decision it needs or the result to accept; this notification alone starts no specialist

For a fixed-time daily standup, use an Ops routine that runs /standup. That is scheduled automation: it needs an awake host and an open window, but does not need JEV to decide that the time has arrived. Bots explains the difference between scheduled and Decision-started runs.

05The launcher

VIKI's launcher is the circle that floats over the window.

  • Move it
    drag it anywhere, or move it with Alt+arrow keys. Reset it with Home.
  • Open the panel
    select it, or press Alt+V from anywhere in the window while no other dialog is open.
  • Close the panel
    Esc closes it again and returns focus to the launcher. When Alt+V opened it, focus returns to wherever you were.
  • Resize the panel
    drag its outer edges. Double-click an edge, or press Enter on it, to restore that side's default. The size is kept.

The launcher's ring shows what's going on without a sound:

  • A gentle brighten
    new information.
  • A number
    waiting items.
  • A pulsing ring
    something it wants to flag.
  • A turning arc
    it's running a chat for you.

The launcher still opens the panel, dimmed, whenever Decision is off or paused.

While plans that VIKI's chats prepared wait for your answer, the panel's top line says so, right after Watching. It reads "1 plan waits for you", or "2 plans wait for you" once more than one do.

06Items

Open the panel to see what VIKI has noticed. Each item carries:

  • a kind chip: For your information, Question, Suggestion, Ready for you or Report;
  • what it's about;
  • a Why now line explaining why it surfaced now;
  • evidence chips linking back to the note or chat behind it;
  • its own actions.

Every item also keeps the same feedback controls:

  • Not now
    sets it aside.
  • Useful
    records that it was right.
  • Not useful
    marks it wrong.
  • Stop these
    in the item's ⋯ menu, mutes that kind of item until you unmute it, with a reason if you give one: Out of date, Already knew, Wrong topic or Bad timing. Unmute it again from How VIKI may reach you.

Useful closes the item, as Not useful does, unless the item still offers a way to start its work:

  • its own start action;
  • one VIKI is about to start under Allowed.

In that case it stays open so you or VIKI can still start it, and its button then reads Marked useful.

What VIKI watches

What VIKI watches on the Decision page starts with How often VIKI checks:

  • About every minute: the default.
  • Every 5 minutes
  • Every 15 minutes

Whichever you pick, VIKI also checks soon after you switch chats or notes, open the launcher or come back to the window.

Under it, ten switches, each on by default, sit in three groups: In your vault, In the app and Improvements. These switches also work with simple rules. Each one turns a group of items on or off:

SwitchWhat VIKI lists while it is on
Tasks dueTasks that are due; with Plan next steps for my projects, a project's overdue tasks; with Self-improvement, proposals in Approvals to archive a project's ticked tasks
InboxCaptures waiting in 00-inbox/; with Suggest destinations for my inbox, inbox suggestions
Vault changesUncommitted changes in a vault kept in Git; with Self-improvement, proposals in Approvals to link two notes or mark an older note as replaced
ApprovalsProposals in Approvals and permission or question cards waiting in your chats, and a chat whose oldest card has waited five minutes or more
Chats and runsAgent runs at work or ready for your review, and messages and MCP servers that need a look
RoutinesYour routines, and your Bots' routine runs waiting for your OK or your answer; the Bot runs VIKI starts or offers follow Start Bots' work instead
Self-improvementOffers to improve VIKI and your vault
KanbanKanban cards that need you or stopped moving
Vault healthStopped saves, deleted notes about to expire, a nearly full store for deleted notes and memories to review
MessagingMessaging bridges that stopped

A switch also gates the work VIKI may start from what it lists. The text beside the switch says so, and so does the matching line in What VIKI may do:

  • Tasks due
    off also stops plans and work chats for due tasks, plans for overdue tasks and proposals to archive ticked tasks. Plans and work chats for due tasks need the Decision model.
  • Inbox
    off also stops inbox suggestions.
  • Vault changes
    off also stops Note links and Superseded notes proposals, which need the Decision model.
  • Self-improvement
    off stops skill suggestions, Sources to learn, feedback reviews and vault upkeep proposals. Sources to learn, Note links and Superseded notes need the Decision model.

Look on my behalf has no watch switch. Vault upkeep proposals also need an ordinary vault and Daily limit: vault changes above 0.

The items for code folders, second looks, project plans, message drafts and saved checks come with their grants in What VIKI may do, as the sections below describe.

Kanban cards

While Kanban is on in What VIKI watches (on by default):

  • Cards that need you
    VIKI lists the cards directly in your vault's kanban/ folder that need you: status: blocked as a Question and status: review as Ready for you.
  • Cards that stopped moving
    it reports, as a Report, a card left working for a day or todo for three days without a change.

Each card item shows the card's title and Open card, which opens its note in the vault view.

  • How many
    VIKI lists at most six cards that need you and three that stopped moving. A card already listed keeps its place, and a new one waits for a free place.
  • Badges and nudges
    a card that needs you stays in the list, with no badge or nudge, until 30 minutes after its last change. One that already shows a badge or nudge keeps it when the card is edited.
  • Reading cards
    VIKI reads the front matter of up to 128 cards each time it checks. A card it could not read keeps its item as it was.

See Bots for the card format.

Bot runs

While Routines is on in What VIKI watches, VIKI also lists the routine runs of your Bots in the open vault.

A run that waits for your OK or your answer shows at once as a Question, such as "Research needs your OK to continue.", with Open session. It closes once you answer.

While Start Bots' work is not Off, VIKI shows:

  • For your information
    a run VIKI started, with Open session and Stop.
  • Suggestion
    a seat VIKI could start, with Start.
  • Report
    when a run VIKI started stopped, reached its time limit, could not start or moved none of its cards. A Report also says why VIKI held a start back: today's limit, the Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage setting, quiet hours, a routine changed since its test, or two routines for one seat.

A report held back by quiet hours or by the plan-usage setting also offers Start, so you can start that seat yourself.

These items stay in the list with no badge or nudge. Only the Decision model can make a waiting run louder.

Vault, chats and bridges

VIKI also lists what it notices elsewhere in the app, each with the place that answers it. Each group below shows while its switch is on in What VIKI watches:

  • Vault health

    on by default. In a vault whose policy is Ordinary, VIKI reports, as a Report:

    • saves stopped because a note operation didn't finish;
    • a save left partway through for two minutes;
    • a deleted note that expires within three days;
    • a nearly full store for deleted notes, which every vault shares.

    It also asks, as a Question, about a memory you approved on this computer that cites a note changed since. Each offers Open vault, where Recovery and Memory hold the answer. Recovery opens by itself while a save is stopped.

  • Approvals

    a chat whose oldest card has waited five minutes or more shows as a Question, oldest first and at most six. The exceptions are a Bot's routine run and a chat VIKI started, which have their own items.

  • Chats and runs

    VIKI reports these, both with Open chat:

    • a message from before VIKI Agent last started, up to a day old when VIKI first checks, whose arrival at Claude Code is unknown;
    • a chat whose last context reading shows one MCP server's loaded tools taking a tenth or more of its context.
  • Messaging

    VIKI reports a messaging bridge that stopped, with Open Messaging.

These items stay in the list with no badge or nudge, start no work, and close once what they report clears.

Code folders

While Look on my behalf is not Off and a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open, VIKI also checks your trusted code folders. It checks one folder at each check, and each folder at most every half hour.

  • When it shows
    a folder whose uncommitted changes to tracked files have not changed for a day or more shows as a Suggestion. New files not yet added to Git and deleted files don't count.
  • Order and limit
    most recently changed first, and at most three.
  • Actions
    Open in Code and, while the grant is Ask first, Take a look.
  • When it closes
    once VIKI has started a chat for it, or once those changes are committed or change again.

Second looks

While Take a second look at my work is not Off and a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open, VIKI watches the chat you have open. It shows these items:

  • Offer
    when a reply there finishes after a long task, or after you corrected VIKI in that chat, and the reply edited notes in the vault, it shows as a Suggestion. It offers Open chat and, while the grant is Ask first, Take a second look. It closes once VIKI has started the second look, or once that chat gets a new reply — even while another chat is the one you have open.
  • Plan waiting
    while a second look's plan waits for you, a Suggestion names what it found: a possible flaw, a better approach or a missing piece. It offers Open plan and closes once you answer the plan.
  • Nothing found
    a second look that finds nothing ends with one quiet Report, such as "Second look at your chat: nothing worth your time.", with Open chat.
  • Could not start or failed
    a second look that could not start or failed still shows a Report.

Project plans

While Plan next steps for my projects is not Off and a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open, VIKI also watches your active projects. These are the overview notes 10-projects/<slug>/<slug>.md whose front matter reads type: project and status: active, up to the eight whose overview changed most recently.

  • Stalled project
    a project none of whose notes has changed for two weeks or more shows as a Suggestion, most recently changed first and at most three.
  • Overdue tasks
    while Tasks due is on in What VIKI watches, so does each project's tasks.md holding an open task three days or more past its due date, among the tasks VIKI lists.
  • Actions
    each offers Open note and, while the grant is Ask first, Plan next steps or Check these tasks.
  • When it closes
    once VIKI has started its chat, or once the project changes or those tasks are ticked or given another date.
  • Held back
    a project or tasks.md that Never send holds back gets no item. Neither does a project with a Never send folder inside it, or a tasks.md with a listed task Never send holds back.
  • Plan waiting
    while such a chat's plan waits for you, a Suggestion says so, with Open plan. It closes once you answer the plan.
  • Could not start or failed
    a project plan that could not start or failed shows a Report.

Message drafts

While Prepare drafts is not Off and a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open, VIKI also offers messages for the chat you have open, when it is your own. It is not your own when it is:

  • VIKI's chat;
  • a chat VIKI started;
  • a routine run;
  • a Bot's or an agent's chat;
  • a chat in a code folder.

Each draft is offered by a Suggestion:

Draft a handoffDraft literature notes
Offered whenClaude Code reports that chat's context 70% full or more at the end of a replyYour last reply there fetched web pages
The message asksFor the decisions, open questions and next stepsClaude Code to write a literature note for each page, and to show you each note and wait for your go-ahead first. If that reply read no note in your vault, the message also asks it to search your notes on the same subject first
Closes onceThat chat is no longer the one you have open or reports less than 70%That reply is no longer the last one in the chat you have open

Draft a handoff puts its message in that chat's message box. Send it, then choose New chat with this turn on the reply to carry on in a fresh chat.

VIKI puts a draft in the message box only when you select it, and sends nothing.

Saved checks

While Run my saved checks is not Off and a vault whose policy is Ordinary is open, VIKI also looks at your trusted code folders that have saved checks. It looks at one folder each time it checks, and at each folder at most every five minutes.

  • When it shows
    a folder has stayed for ten minutes at a commit that a saved check you have run in that folder before has not run on. A Suggestion says so, for at most three folders.
  • Actions
    Open in Code and, while the grant is Ask first, Run checks.
  • While the checks run
    the item is For your information, with Stop.
  • After you stop them
    once you stop them, or press Stop all after VIKI began starting them, VIKI starts no further check on that commit by itself while VIKI Agent stays open.
  • When they end
    a Report says whether they passed, one failed, or they did not finish.
  • A check VIKI could not start
    makes that report say they did not finish, unless one failed. VIKI does not try it again on that commit while VIKI Agent stays open; the Checks tab still runs it.
  • When it closes
    once the folder moves to another commit.

The item names the folder, not its checks. The Code workbench's Checks tab shows each check and its output.

Inbox suggestions

While Suggest destinations for my inbox is not Off, Inbox is on in What VIKI watches and a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open, VIKI also looks at the captures in 00-inbox/.

A Suggestion tells you when all of these hold:

  • the inbox has more than three captures, or one older than three days;
  • some captures have no suggested destination;
  • no suggestion run has started since the newest capture changed;
  • the newest capture has not changed for ten minutes.

The item offers Triage inbox and, while the grant is Ask first, Suggest destinations, which starts the same run as Ask VIKI to suggest.

  • While that run goes
    the item is For your information.
  • Once suggestions wait
    it is Ready for you.
  • When the run could not suggest
    a Report says so.
  • When a run finds no destination it can use
    the run ends its item.

Triage inbox opens the triage, where you choose each capture's destination and send the filing draft. Nothing in your vault changes until you do.

VIKI starts one run for each state of the inbox, whatever its result, while VIKI Agent stays open. A capture added, changed or filed makes a new state, and the item closes.

07VIKI's chat

At the bottom of the panel is VIKI's own chat, a Message VIKI box kept separate from your regular chats. Send it a message to start a conversation.

  • New conversation
    clears it so your next message starts fresh.
  • Open in main window
    continues that same chat there. VIKI's replies here have no Read aloud button; use Open in main window to hear them.

With dictation available, the box also offers the microphone and the round Hands-free button (Alt+T), and your first words start the chat.

While talking to VIKI, the first Esc ends the conversation and keeps the panel open. The next Esc closes the panel.

  • Closing the panel
    however it closes, ends a voice conversation still running.
  • Opening the panel
    ends a voice conversation running in your main chat instead.

08What leaves this computer

The What leaves this computer row controls what Decision may send.

  • Send level
    picks how much: Titles only, Titles and short excerpts (up to 200 characters) (the default) or Titles and sections (up to 2,000 characters).
  • Never send
    add a folder ending in / or a tag starting with # (one written inline counts too). VIKI leaves anything under such a folder or tag out before anything is sent. It also tells you from how many of today's requests it held something back.
  • See the last state sent
    select it to read the exact text, in Context & loadout's Decision tab.

By kind of item

These kinds of item follow their own rules for what reaches the Decision model.

Important

A chat VIKI starts is a Claude Code chat like your own. It sends what it reads to Anthropic, as your chats do.

  • Kanban cards
    with any tag on Never send, or kanban/ as a folder there, card items stay out of every request and VIKI's own rules list them.
  • Bot runs
    a Bot's item sends only its kind to the Decision model. The seat, the routine and its cards stay on this computer.
  • Vault, chats and bridges
    the items VIKI notices elsewhere in the app send only their kind to the Decision model. For a waiting chat, the item also sends the kind of card and roughly how long it has waited. The notes, memories, chats, messages, servers and bridges stay on this computer.
  • Code folders
    a code folder's item sends only its kind to the Decision model, never the folder or its changes. A chat VIKI starts in the folder sends what it reads to Anthropic, as your chats do.
  • Second looks
    a second look's items send only their kind and your chat's title to the Decision model, never the notes or the chat.
    • Its message
      the second look's own message names your chat's title and the notes the reply edited, never the chat's text.
    • Held notes
      the message leaves out a note under a Never send folder. With every such note held back, no second look starts.
    • Tags
      a Never send tag is not judged for these notes.
    • Vaults kept in Git
      the chat reads git status and git diff, which can show changes under a held folder.
  • Project plans
    a project plan's items send only their kind to the Decision model, never the project, its notes or its tasks. The plan's own message names one note in your vault, the project's note or its tasks.md, never the note's text.
  • Message drafts
    a message draft's item sends only its kind to the Decision model, never the chat, its pages or its notes. The draft is fixed text with no note, web address or chat text in it. It stays on this computer until you send it, then goes to the selected model provider through Claude Code like any message you write.
  • Saved checks
    a saved-check item sends only its kind to the Decision model, never the folder, its commit or its checks. VIKI reads no check's name, command or output. A check it runs is your own command, run on this computer as Run in the Checks tab runs it.
  • Inbox suggestions
    an inbox suggestion item sends only its kind to the Decision model, never your captures, their names or how many there are.
    • The suggestion run
      a suggestion run VIKI starts is the one Ask VIKI to suggest starts. It sends the name, the captured value and the first 600 characters of each capture in 00-inbox/, up to 100 of them, and your project names to Claude. It can read files in your vault with its read-only tools.
    • When VIKI starts no run
      with Never send holding any tag, a folder over a capture in 00-inbox/, or a folder in 10-projects/ (the run also sends your project names). Your own Ask VIKI to suggest still starts one.
    • When the inbox changes after VIKI last listed it
      a run started from VIKI's launcher stops before it sends anything. The next check applies Never send to the new inbox.

09How VIKI may reach you

Open How VIKI may reach you to set how loud VIKI may be. A legend at the top explains the four ways an item can reach you:

  • Listed
    added to the launcher's list, and the launcher brightens briefly.
  • Badge
    a number on the launcher.
  • Nudge
    the launcher's ring pulses once.
  • Alert
    the ring stays lit until you open the panel.

Badges, nudges and alerts need the Decision model. While VIKI uses simple rules, the row says so and VIKI only lists items.

  • Nudges per hour
    the most nudges and alerts in any hour. 0 means none.
  • Alerts
    on or off. An alert also needs no quiet hours, and a task linked to an active project that is due within 2 hours or overdue.
  • Tell me when I open the related chat or note
    VIKI may hold an item until you open the chat or note it is about.
  • Quiet hours
    no nudges or alerts. VIKI also holds its own looks, second looks, project plans, saved checks and inbox runs, and Bots start only routines that stop at a draft. The setting is shared with Routines.
  • Topics you stopped
    the kinds you muted with Stop these, each with a way to unmute it. With none stopped, the row says so.

The Focus button on the Proactive VIKI card holds nudges and alerts for an hour, as quiet hours do.

10What VIKI may do

Open What VIKI may do to set its grants. One legend at the top explains the three choices for every grant:

  • Off
    VIKI doesn't start it.
  • Ask first
    offers it as an action on its item in VIKI's launcher.
  • Allowed
    lets VIKI start it at its next check, within the daily limit.

Message drafts are the exception: they wait for you to select them under Ask first and Allowed alike.

The row lists each kind of work on its own line, with its daily limit and today's count beside it. The longer explanation of a line sits under More about this. The lines come in groups:

  • Running chats
    first, and only while something runs, the chats VIKI started.
  • Prepared for your review
    nothing changes until you approve. Prepare drafts, Look on my behalf, Take a second look at my work, Plan next steps for my projects, Suggest destinations for my inbox and Vault upkeep proposals (with Daily limit: vault changes).
  • Work that can make changes
    chats use your usual Claude Code permissions, Bot runs use their routine's settings, and saved checks are your own commands. Start chats to do work, Start Bots' work (with Let seats hand work to each other under it) and Run my saved checks.
  • Safety
    Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage.

The default daily limits are five prepared drafts and three work chats, counted across workspaces.

A line also says when a grant cannot start work, for each case that applies:

  • Needs the Decision model
    plans and work chats for due tasks, and Note links and Superseded notes proposals. The other grants also work with simple rules.
  • A watch switch is off
    Tasks due off leaves no plans or work chats for due tasks and no plans for overdue tasks. Inbox off leaves no inbox suggestions. Self-improvement off leaves no upkeep. Vault changes off leaves no Note links or Superseded notes, and Tasks due off leaves no archiving of ticked tasks.
GrantWhat VIKI may start or offerDefaultDaily limit (default, from 0 to 10)Vault policy
Prepare draftsA plan for a due task, in a chat that waits for your approval; message drafts for the chat you have openAllowedDaily limit: drafts (5); Daily limit: message drafts (3)Ordinary or Protected
Start chats to do workA chat that does a due task under your normal permission promptsAsk firstDaily limit: chats (3)Ordinary
Start Bots' workA seat's tested routine set to Only when a card is waitingAsk firstDaily limit: Bot runs VIKI starts (4)Ordinary
Look on my behalfA plan-mode chat in a trusted code folder whose changes have sat for a dayAllowedDaily limit: looks VIKI starts (3)Ordinary or Protected
Take a second look at my workA plan-mode chat after a long or corrected reply that edited notesAllowedDaily limit: second looks VIKI starts (3)Ordinary or Protected

Vault policy is the policy of the vault you have open; Vault policy below explains it. Daily limit: vault changes caps the vault-upkeep proposals, which wait in Approvals instead.

Chats VIKI starts

At most two chats that Decision starts run at once, each against its own daily limit. VIKI starts none of its own while one is open, so one stays free for yours.

  • Session list
    a chat VIKI started shows a Started by VIKI chip in your session list.
  • Stop and Stop all
    stop one on its own with Stop, or all together with Stop all. Stop all also keeps VIKI from starting chats or Bot runs of its own for one check interval after you press it, as How often VIKI checks sets it.
  • When it ends
    a chat VIKI started that finishes, fails or reaches its time limit while you have answered none of its cards closes, even while you are looking at it. It reopens from its transcript when you select it in your session list. One you answered a card in or stopped stays open.
  • Once you stop one
    VIKI does not start work for that item again on its own, even after the item changes.
  • Before each start
    just before each chat, Bot run, saved check or inbox suggestion run it starts on its own, VIKI reads your settings, quiet hours and plan use again. It starts nothing while proactivity is off or paused or no app window is open, so a change you save while it checks holds that start.

VIKI starts a Bot only through its own tested routine, under Start Bots' work. Apart from the notice of a Bot whose delivery you turned on, it does not message other chats or people or send to your phone.

Held starts and daily limits

While VIKI holds back its own start of an item under Allowed, that item offers its start as under Ask first instead. Its Why now line names what is holding it and says you can start it yourself. A start is held back when:

  • another chat VIKI started is open;
  • Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds it;
  • it's your quiet hours;
  • VIKI is waiting for a better moment.

At today's daily limit for that kind of work, the item offers no start at all. That limit counts the ones you start yourself too. Its Why now line says the limit is reached and that you can raise it here, in What VIKI may do.

Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage

Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage picks Off, 50%, 80% (the default) or 95%.

  • At the share you pick
    while a plan window Claude Code reported, whose reset is still ahead, is at that share of your plan or more, VIKI starts no chat on its own.
  • At your plan limit
    while your plan limit is reached, VIKI holds those chats until that limit resets, whatever you pick here.
  • Before Claude Code reports
    until Claude Code first reports your plan use after VIKI Agent starts, VIKI holds every start this setting holds, whatever you pick here, Off included.

A chat it holds back is not stored and does not count against a daily limit, so VIKI starts it at its first check after the hold ends. While it holds them, What VIKI may do reads Holding and says until when.

Your own Prepare a plan and Start a chat to do it are not held.

Start Bots' work

Start Bots' work picks Off, Ask first (the default) or Allowed. It applies when both of these hold:

  • one of your todo cards directly in the vault's kanban/ folder waits for a seat (its owner/<seat> tag);
  • that seat has exactly one enabled routine set to Only when a card is waiting, tested at its current version.

Then Allowed starts that routine at VIKI's next check, and Ask first offers Start in the launcher.

  • Your cards
    a card counts as yours when it last changed outside every routine run and every chat VIKI started. A card written during one gets Start instead, unless Let seats hand work to each other is on (off by default).
  • After a run
    VIKI starts the seat again only when one of its cards that is not todo changed during that run, or when you add or change one of its todo cards.
  • After Stop or Stop all
    after you Stop such a run, or press Stop all, Allowed starts that seat again only once you add or change one of its todo cards. Ask first keeps offering Start.
  • Future file times
    a todo card whose file time is ahead of this computer's clock counts only once that time comes.

Daily limit: Bot runs VIKI starts, 4 by default and from 0 to 10, counts across workspaces. It includes the runs you start with Start and leaves out a run that could not start.

  • Running beside other runs
    VIKI starts a Bot on its own only while no routine run is going, so a scheduled routine finds a free place. Your own Start can run beside one other run.
  • Nothing starts
    while two routine runs are going, while Pause all holds your routines, or outside a vault whose policy is Ordinary.
  • Holds
    Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds these starts too. In your quiet hours VIKI starts only routines set to Stop at a draft; a question in such a run still waits until its time limit. Neither holds your own Start.
  • A run VIKI starts
    keeps its routine's prompt, time limit, confirmation setting and Bot notice, and passes the checks a scheduled run passes. It reads Started by VIKI in its run history and your session list. Stop on its item or Stop all here stops it.

Bots explains how to set up seats and cards.

Look on my behalf

Look on my behalf picks Off, Ask first or Allowed (the default). When one of your trusted code folders has uncommitted changes to tracked files that have not changed for a day or more:

  • Allowed
    starts a chat in that folder at VIKI's next check.
  • Ask first
    offers Take a look in the launcher.

VIKI starts the chat in plan mode and asks it to look the changes over and present what is half-done or risky as a plan. VIKI asks the plan to lead with what it found and, in at most five numbered steps, what approving does, with its evidence under a closing Details heading that the card folds shut until you open it. The chat waits for your approval before it changes anything. VIKI starts one such chat for each state of a folder's changes.

Daily limit: looks VIKI starts, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts across workspaces and includes the chats you start with Take a look.

  • Vault policy
    VIKI checks code folders only while a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected is open.
  • Holds
    Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds these chats too, and VIKI starts none in your quiet hours. Neither holds your own Take a look.

Take a second look at my work

Take a second look at my work picks Off, Ask first or Allowed (the default). When a reply in the chat you have open finishes a long task, or work you corrected in that chat, and edited notes in the vault:

  • Allowed
    starts a chat in plan mode at VIKI's next check.
  • Ask first
    offers Take a second look.

VIKI asks that chat to read those notes and present at most one flaw, better approach or missing piece as a plan. VIKI asks the plan to lead with a heading naming the finding, why it matters and, in at most five numbered steps, what approving does, with its evidence under a closing Details heading that the card folds shut until you open it. The chat waits for your approval before it changes anything. On that plan:

  • Approve
    makes the change.
  • Keep planning
    turns it down only if that chat then ends without your approval, so approving it later in the same chat still counts as approved.

VIKI takes at most one second look at each reply, and none at a chat VIKI started, a routine run, a Bot's or an agent's chat, or a chat in a code folder.

Daily limit: second looks VIKI starts, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts across workspaces and includes the chats you start with Take a second look.

Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds these chats too, and VIKI starts none in your quiet hours. Neither holds your own Take a second look.

Plan next steps for my projects

Plan next steps for my projects picks Off, Ask first or Allowed (the default). When nothing in one of your active projects has changed for two weeks, or a project's tasks are three days or more overdue:

  • Allowed
    starts a chat in plan mode in the vault at VIKI's next check.
  • Ask first
    offers Plan next steps or Check these tasks.

VIKI asks that chat to read the project's note or its tasks.md, and to present one of these as a plan:

  • three next actions for the project;
  • ticks for the overdue tasks that look done, and new dates for the rest.

VIKI asks each plan to open with a line on where things stand — the project overall, or how many tasks look done and how many need a new date — before that list, with its reasons under a closing Details heading that the card folds shut until you open it. The chat waits for your approval before it changes anything. On that plan:

  • Approve
    makes the change.
  • Keep planning
    turns it down only if that chat then ends without your approval, so approving it later in the same chat still counts as approved.

VIKI starts one such chat each time a project stalls, and one for each set of overdue tasks. While one is open, VIKI starts no other chat of its own, in any vault, until you answer or stop it.

Daily limit: project plans VIKI starts, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts across workspaces and includes the chats you start from these items.

Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds these chats too, and VIKI starts none in your quiet hours. Neither holds your own start.

Prepare drafts and message drafts

Prepare drafts also lets VIKI offer message drafts for the chat you have open, as Message drafts above describes. Under Ask first and Allowed alike, a draft waits in VIKI's launcher until you select it. Off offers none.

Daily limit: message drafts, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts each new draft VIKI raises in a day, across workspaces. It includes one VIKI decides not to show you, and never drops a draft already raised.

  • Muted kinds
    a kind you turned off with Stop these is not raised at all.
  • Plan usage
    message drafts start no chat, so Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage does not apply to them.

Run my saved checks

Run my saved checks picks Off, Ask first (the default) or Allowed. When a trusted code folder stays for ten minutes at a commit that some of its saved checks have not run on, including a commit a pull brought in:

  • Allowed
    runs, the next time VIKI checks, each of those checks you have run in that folder before, as Run in the Checks tab does.
  • Ask first
    offers Run checks in the launcher.

Warning

Each check is your own command, run with your account's rights in the folder itself: it can change files and use the network.

VIKI runs a check at most once on each commit, whatever its result. It does not run a check you have not run in that folder before, and runs none while a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is under way.

Daily limit: new commits VIKI checks, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts each folder commit VIKI raises in a day, across workspaces. It includes one VIKI decides not to show you and the ones you run with Run checks.

  • Muted kinds
    a kind you turned off with Stop these is not raised at all.
  • Vault policy
    VIKI runs or offers these checks only while a vault whose policy is Ordinary is open.
  • Holds
    VIKI runs none in your quiet hours. Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage does not apply, since checks use no plan. Neither holds your own Run checks.
  • Stopping
    Stop on the item, or Stop all here, cancels the check runs started from VIKI while VIKI Agent stays open. VIKI then starts no more checks of its own on that commit, as Saved checks above describes.

Suggest destinations for my inbox

Suggest destinations for my inbox picks Off, Ask first or Allowed (the default). When an inbox item is due, as Inbox suggestions above describes:

  • Allowed
    starts the inbox's suggestion run at VIKI's next check.
  • Ask first
    offers Suggest destinations in the launcher.

The run is the one Ask VIKI to suggest starts:

  • it is one reply from Claude Code with only Read, Glob and Grep and no MCP server;
  • it is ended after five minutes;
  • it denies any permission it asks for;
  • it changes nothing;
  • its suggestions are kept after VIKI Agent restarts.

VIKI remembers each inbox state it started a run for after a restart too, so it does not run the same state again. Under Allowed, a state it raised before a restart and never started starts at its next check.

Daily limit: inbox suggestion items, 3 by default and from 0 to 10, counts each inbox state VIKI raises in a day, across workspaces. It includes one VIKI decides not to show you and the ones you start with Suggest destinations.

  • Muted kinds
    a kind you turned off with Stop these is not raised at all.
  • Holds
    VIKI starts none in your quiet hours, and Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage holds these runs too. Neither holds your own Suggest destinations or Ask VIKI to suggest.
  • Once per inbox
    VIKI does not start the run again for the same inbox, even when it failed. After VIKI Agent restarts, it starts none for an inbox it raised before, whose item then offers Suggest destinations under Allowed too. Ask VIKI to suggest in the triage runs it again as well.
  • Older file times
    a capture moved or synced into 00-inbox/ with a file time older than the last run waits for the next newer change.
  • Stopping
    a run VIKI starts shows no Started by VIKI chip, and Stop and Stop all do not reach it. It ends by itself within five minutes.

Vault policy

What VIKI starts and offers depends on the policy of the vault you have open:

  • Protected
    VIKI only prepares plans: it starts and offers no work chat, whatever Start chats to do work says.
  • Read-only (existing folder)
    VIKI starts and offers no plan and no work chat.

Self-improvement drafts that wait for you to send them still come in every vault. Message drafts still come in a vault whose policy is Ordinary or Protected.

VIKI reads the vault's policy at each check, so a change applies from the next one. Your own Prepare a plan or Start a chat to do it reads it when you select it.

11Learning

The History and learning group contains Learning. Its feedback guide explains Useful, Not useful and Stop these.

  • Learning details and statistics
    open it for the numeric breakdowns.
  • Comparison
    the optional comparison with another model version sits under Decision model › Advanced: version and comparison, not here.

Open Learning, between How VIKI is doing and Data, to see what VIKI has learned from your answers:

  • Useful, Not useful and Stop these;
  • opening or acting on an item;
  • the weekly check below.

Turn it on or off with its switch. Either way, this only changes how loud and when VIKI speaks up, never your limits. Quiet hours, nudges per hour, alerts, muted topics and what VIKI may do stay as you set them.

From the first decisions, Learning tunes only when and how loudly VIKI speaks up. Once it has 20 labels, including at least three positive and three negative, it also learns which questions and topics matter to you.

Select any of these:

  • Show all numbers
    for a table of every number next to where it started.
  • How well it matches you
    for how VIKI's confidence compares with your own feedback.
  • Each question
    for that same comparison broken down by what VIKI asked.

How VIKI's own work went

Learning also shows how the work VIKI starts or offers on its own went, each over the last 30 days and since your last Reset:

  • Second looks
    for a long task and for a correction, how many second looks VIKI started and how many you approved or turned down. It also shows the reasons you gave with Not useful on their items, and how many found nothing.
    • A second look that finds nothing does not count toward pausing that kind, though it still shows here as found nothing.
    • Once 10 of one kind of second look were approved or turned down, VIKI stops taking that kind while fewer than 1 in 4 of those was approved. It says so and offers Try again.
    • VIKI also stops raising a kind of finding you turned down 5 times in a row, and offers Show these again.
  • Project plans
    for a stalled project and for overdue tasks, how many plans VIKI started and how many you approved or turned down. It also shows the reasons you gave with Not useful on their items, and how many found nothing to propose.
    • Once 10 of one kind were answered or found nothing, VIKI stops that kind while fewer than 1 in 4 is approved. It says so and offers Try again.
  • Message drafts
    for a nearly full chat and for fetched pages, how many drafts VIKI's launcher showed you and how many you used or turned down. It also shows the reasons you gave with Not useful, and how many closed before you used or answered them.
    • Selecting a draft's button counts as using it.
    • Once 10 of one kind were used, turned down or closed, VIKI stops offering that kind while fewer than 1 in 4 is used. It says so and offers Try again.
  • Saved checks
    how many new-commit items VIKI's launcher showed you, and how many you used, by selecting Run checks or Useful, or turned down. It also shows the reasons you gave with Not useful.
    • Once 10 were used or turned down, VIKI stops raising them while fewer than 1 in 4 is used. It says so and offers Try again.
    • An item you leave unanswered counts toward neither.
  • Inbox suggestions
    how many inbox suggestion items VIKI's launcher showed you, and how many you used, by selecting Triage inbox or Suggest destinations on the item or Useful, or turned down. It also shows the reasons you gave with Not useful, and how many runs found no destination VIKI could use.
    • Once 10 were used, turned down or found nothing, VIKI stops raising them while fewer than 1 in 4 is used. It says so and offers Try again.
    • An item you leave unanswered counts toward neither.

None of these pauses changes your grant, daily limit or quiet hours. Delete all decision history forgets these counts. Deleting decisions or suggestions recounts them.

Comparison and reset

Compare with another model version sits under Decision model › Advanced: version and comparison, and is off until you turn it on. When you set it to Pinned, Latest stable or Preview, every new decision is also asked of that version, for comparison only: its answers never change what VIKI decides.

Important

Each comparison is a second paid call within the same daily cap and 10-a-minute limit. If TypeSafe rejects your key or says it is busy, VIKI pauses all its requests, live ones included.

Select Reset what VIKI learned to start its numbers over from scratch. Your decisions and labels stay.

12Weekly check

While some of last week's held-back items are still unlabelled, a Weekly check card appears in the launcher panel. It names how many things VIKI held back and asks whether that was right.

  • Check
    opens it inside How VIKI is doing.
  • Skip this week
    dismisses the card until next week.

There, Weekly check lists up to 10 of last week's held-back items, picked at random. When none were held back, it says there's nothing to check. Each item gets the same two choices:

  • Right to hold
    confirms VIKI was right to stay quiet.
  • Should have told me
    marks it as a miss.

How VIKI is doing is mostly a record to read:

  • Last 30 days
    counts what VIKI showed you and how you answered.
  • See every decision in Data
    opens the full decision list.
  • See how you answered, day by day
    opens the answer history.

Only two parts need you:

  • Weekly check
    asks once a week. The row's status shows how many items are left to check, or Nothing to do now.
  • Report a missing suggestion
    found under Something VIKI missed, and optional at any time. It counts as one Should have told me in the 30-day numbers and does not record what was missed.

While Learning is on, it uses your weekly check answers to tune when and how loudly VIKI speaks up.

13Self-improvement

VIKI also watches for ways to improve itself, and raises what it finds through the same launcher as everything else:

  • an offer to turn a chat into a skill;
  • one of your own skills that fits the chat you're in;
  • a captured source that may be worth a literature note;
  • a suggestion to run a retro once several items are marked Not useful;
  • better wording for one of Decision's own questions;
  • three kinds of vault upkeep: linking two notes, marking an older note as replaced by a newer one, and archiving a project's ticked tasks.

Drafts and skill suggestions

The first five only prepare a draft in a chat, and nothing is sent until you press Send yourself.

  • Use this skill
    a skill that fits has this one action, which puts its / command there instead. It is offered at most once a chat, and never for one already used there.
  • Stop these
    on a skill that fits, mutes only Skill suggestions.

A skill offer's reason shows as that item's Why now line in the launcher, not under the chat reply.

Vault-upkeep proposals

The three vault-upkeep kinds skip the draft in a chat and land straight in Approvals instead, as a Link proposal or Upkeep proposal row. Only once you select Approve there does VIKI make a draft of that one edit. Nothing in the vault changes until you send it.

The three vault-upkeep kinds come only from a vault whose policy is Ordinary. A vault whose policy is Protected or Read-only (existing folder) gets no new ones, and one filed while the vault was Ordinary stays in Approvals.

Daily limit: vault changes is a setting beside the drafts and chats limits in What VIKI may do. It caps the three vault-upkeep kinds together: 0 to 10 a day, 3 by default, and 0 turns vault-change proposals off. It's one count across every workspace, not per workspace.

Self-improvement settings

  • Self-improvement
    this switch, in What VIKI watches, turns every kind off together. It is on by default.
  • Stop these
    on any one item, mutes just that kind, the same as for any other item.
  • Vault-upkeep kinds
    these have no launcher item, so Daily limit: vault changes at 0 stops them.

Whatever these settings say, each request to the Decision model also carries:

  • the titles of notes changed since yesterday, and of items Decision showed you in the last day;
  • the items you most recently marked mute or wrong;
  • your recent feedback.

These are titles only, never a note's own text, and Never send applies to them as to everything else.

14Better questions

Decision's own questions can be reworded too.

  1. The better-wording item's draft asks, in a chat, for new wording for one question.
  2. Once a reply gives it in the shape asked for, that reply offers Propose this wording, sending it to Approvals.
  3. Once proposed, every fresh decision also asks the proposed wording once, in the shadow, as a second paid call within the same daily cap and 10-a-minute limit. Its answers never change what VIKI decides, and only one wording is tried at a time.
  4. From Approvals, Approve switches new decisions to it and asks every item still open one more time under the new wording.
  5. Once a wording is in use, the same row offers Undo to go back to the one before it.

Delete all decision history forgets the trial numbers behind this comparison, not the wording itself.

15Data

Open Data to see What VIKI keeps for this workspace. Each card shows its count, oldest and newest date, and limit:

  • Decision history
    decisions and reports, newest 10,000 from up to 365 days.
  • Suggestions
    up to 50 open; closed suggestions are kept for 30 days.
  • Model calls
    the newest 20.
  • Chats VIKI started
    no limit. VIKI keeps these so it does not start the same work twice. You cannot delete them here; their transcripts stay in Claude Code.
  • Proposals
    up to 50 wordings and 50 vault changes. Act on them in Approvals.
  • Learned preferences
    reset them together with Reset what VIKI learned. Unmute a topic in Topics you stopped.
  • Decision model key
    one key for every workspace; change it in Decision model.

Activity shows Last 30 days, Last 90 days or Last 365 days. The chart uses a column per day, or per week for 365 days. Select Show as table for its values. How you answered uses the same days. Topics covers every stored decision.

Browse and delete lists decisions, suggestions or model calls. Filter the first two lists and show 50 rows at a time with Show 50 more. Model calls appear all at once. Open Details on a row; model call details include its model version and answers. Open in Context shows what VIKI sent in each model call.

Select up to 50 rows with Delete selected, or delete every matching decision or suggestion. The count is fixed when Data loads. Rows still in use stay and explain why: a decision stays while its suggestion is open; a suggestion stays while it is open or a chat VIKI started holds it. Each confirmation lists what else changes and what stays. Deleting decisions waits for VIKI's current check to stop and resets what VIKI learned. Delete all decision history removes decisions and reports, every suggestion, every model call and what VIKI learned.

Its confirmation also explains that paused kinds are counted again; today's message drafts, saved checks and inbox suggestions get their counts back; today's looks, second looks and project plans count toward Daily limit: drafts until tomorrow; comparisons lose their numbers; an approved or rejected vault change teaches VIKI nothing; and self-improvement suggestions are worked out again. Settings, grants, Topics you stopped, chats VIKI started and their transcripts, proposals, wording in use, today's call count and spending stay. A deleted item marked Not useful can return, and VIKI may start its work again.
